benchmarks.task_description:
fix(shell): keep execute output when a byte does not decode

## Description

On macOS and Linux, and on Windows without Git Bash, the agent's `execute` decoded command output with the locale encoding in strict mode, so one byte that does not decode, as in `cat` of a Latin-1 file or a program that prints raw bytes, broke the result. On macOS and Linux the whole call failed with `Error executing command (UnicodeDecodeError): …` and exit code 1: the rest of the output and the command's real exit code were lost, and for a command that had timed out so were the 124 and the recovery hint. On Windows the output stream holding the byte came back empty. Under Git Bash on Windows the output was already decoded with `errors="replace"`.

`ShellLaunch.text_options` now adds `errors="replace"` for every shell and keeps the encoding as it was: UTF-8 under Git Bash, the locale default otherwise, so cmd.exe output in a local code page still decodes. A byte that does not decode becomes `�` and the rest of the result comes back as before; `run_in_background` logs are already read this way.

A real `EvoSci -p` run asking the agent to `cat` a Latin-1 file: on `main` the agent gets the `UnicodeDecodeError` and exit code 1; here it gets `Temperature: 25�C` / `R�sum� done` and exit code 0.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] New feature — link issue: #
- [ ] Documentation / examples
- [ ] Test improvement
- [ ] Refactor (no behavior change)

## Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](../CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] This targets **core functionality** used by the majority of users (niche features belong in [EvoSkills](https://github.com/EvoScientist/EvoSkills))
- [x] I have added/updated tests where applicable
- [x] `uv run ruff check .` passes
- [x] `uv run pytest` passes

benchmarks.task_description:
fix: hide host node_modules of mounted MFEs behind a volume

#### WIP -> The jobs run on tutor dev only

### Description
These code changes introduce improvements to the Tutor MFE (Micro-Frontend) plugin by adding automation and efficiency for managing and running tasks in environments where MFEs are mounted. When MFEs are mounted, it will run `npm clean-install` as part of the run `tutor dev launch`. The "mfe" init task `npm-install.sh` is taking care of installing the node_modules, as it is done in the [LMS](https://github.com/overhangio/tutor/blob/master/tutor/templates/jobs/init/mounted-directories.sh)

### Test Cases:
- [x] It will run the `npm-install` script when MFEs are **implicitly** and **expicitly** mounted using the Tutor format: `tutor mounts add $(pwd)/frontend-app-*` & `tutor mounts add [mfe-name]:$(pwd)/frontend-app-*:/openedx/app`.
- [x] The job should run for all mounted MFEs
- [x] The job will run only in `tutor dev`, not `tutor local`, as MFEs mount only in `tutor dev` environment.
- [x] If no `node_modules` are present, it should install `node_modules`.
- [x] If the `node_modules` directory exists but is empty or outdated, it should install `node_modules`.
- [x] If the `package-lock.json` file changes slightly, it should trigger reinstallation of `node_modules`.
- [x] If `node_modules` are installed and then reinstallation is attempted without changes to `package-lock.json`, it should **not** reinstall `node_modules`.

Closes #218 

Special thanks to @Danyal-Faheem for collaborating with me on this and helping to reach a solution. 🙌

benchmarks.task_description:
Add the description required by the applications-download schema

## Summary

Add the `description` required by the `applications-download` schema to `ci/applications.yaml`, and point the `$schema` comment at the current schema.

## Context

- The `Update ngeo` workflows fail on the stabilization branches with `-- ci/applications.yaml:4:3 transifex/cli: 'description' is a required property (rule: additionalProperties.required)`, on the `applications-download --applications=ci/applications.yaml --versions=ci/applications-versions.yaml install --all` step, see https://github.com/camptocamp/c2cgeoportal/actions/runs/40131390022.
- Those workflows check out the stabilization branch, `ref: ${{ env.MAIN_BRANCH }}`, so the validated file is the one of this branch. `master` and `2.10` already have the `description`, the branches `2.7`, `2.8` and `2.9` don't.
- The `$schema` comment pointed to `camptocamp/c2cciutils/master/c2cciutils/schema-applications.json`, which answers `404` since the applications configuration moved to `sbrunner/applications-download`, whose schema answers `200`.
- Related ticket: C2CSEC-185

## Implementation Details

- `ci/applications.yaml` is aligned on the `master` version: `description: Transifex CLI client` is added to the `transifex/cli` application, and the `$schema` comment points to the `applications-download` schema.

## Impact/Risks

- The `Update ngeo` workflow can run again on this branch, it was failing before the `applications-download` installation.
- No functional change, the Transifex CLI installation itself is unchanged.

benchmarks.task_description:
Keep achromatic HSL gradients finite

## Problem

`rgb_to_hsl` masks achromatic hue/saturation outputs after dividing by the zero colour range. The forward value for a grey pixel is correct, but reverse differentiation produces NaNs, including in the lightness component. Low-precision black/white pixels also need a safe denominator for the inactive saturation branch.

## Change

Replace inactive denominators before division, preserving the existing achromatic output branches and chromatic formula. This follows the [JAX guidance on masked undefined operations](https://docs.jax.dev/en/latest/faq.html#gradients-contain-nan-where-using-where).

## Validation

- Earlier full colour-conversion run: **171 passed, 40 skipped** (JAX 0.7.0, TensorFlow 2.20.0).
- Current rebased head: **9** HSL regressions and **20** adjacent conversion tests passed; **5 skipped** (JAX 0.12.0, TensorFlow 2.21.0). Tests now live in `dm_pix/_src/color_conversion_test.py`. Unchanged production code fails eight cases and passes the chromatic finite-difference control.
- Coverage includes black/grey/white, float16/bfloat16/float32, eager/JIT execution, forward/reverse differentiation along the greyscale path, mixed images, and chromatic gradients compared with independent `colorsys` finite differences.
- Python syntax and `git diff --check` pass on the current head.

Hue is mathematically undefined on the achromatic axis. The tests preserve the existing constant hue/saturation branches and verify the lightness derivative along the greyscale path; they do not assert a unique full colour-space derivative there.

Python 3.12.14 on macOS arm64 CPU. GPU/TPU and the complete image-processing suite were not run. Channel-axis handling in #125 is separate and unchanged. No epsilon, colour convention, dependency, or public API changes.

Reproduced against `ffb65074b39b67e1a686d1348f2d461c7ff3ab45`.
